paper_metadata.title: Comparative Study of Quantum-Circuit Scalability in a Financial Problem

summary: This paper studies quantum amplitude estimation for a simplified Treasury bill pricing problem, using a 3-evaluation-qubit example with p = 0.2 and 10,000 simulator shots, and then scales the circuit from 1 to 19 evaluation qubits. It reports two-qubit-gate counts of 12 for an ideal IBM layout, 15 for IBM Yorktown, 23 for IBM Tokyo in a nonideal placement, and 9 for IonQ, with fitted scaling of n^2 for IonQ, n^2 + n for ideal IBM, 2.1n^2 - 4.7n + 6.8 for IBM Tokyo, and 3.5n^2 - 12.8n + 22.3 for IBM Cairo.

experiments.description: Scalability study of quantum amplitude estimation for T-Bill expectation-value estimation, comparing two-qubit gate growth across IBM superconducting devices and IonQ trapped-ion hardware for 1 to 19 evaluation qubits.

algorithm.variant: quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) via simplified QPE
algorithm.parameter_initialization: State preparation via A = RY(theta) with theta = 2 asin(sqrt(p)); no variational optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Single objective qubit encodes bond value probabilities; evaluation register of n qubits controls Q operator in QPE-based QAE
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate expectation value V = (1-p)V_low + pV_high for T-Bill pricing; simplified example uses V_low = $0 and V_high = $1 so V = p

problem_instance.description: Treasury bill (T-Bill) expectation-value estimation / bond pricing under a single-period binomial model

dataset_specification.description: Single-period binomial model with probability p; example uses p = 0.2

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No dataset preprocessing; probability encoded directly into a single-qubit rotation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit resource counting across 1 to 19 evaluation qubits; example simulation run with 10,000 shots on IBM QASM simulator; polynomial fits to two-qubit gate counts

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM superconducting backends and IonQ trapped-ion gate decompositions via Qiskit transpile

transpilation_settings.routing_method: transpile-dependent; SABRE mentioned as possible mapper

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classically select most probable measurement outcome and convert estimated probability to bond value

results.unit: probability / estimated price in simplified $0-$1 bond example

classical_baselines.unit: probability / price units in simplified example

speedup_claims.conditions: for expectation-value estimation with QAE, using M = 2^n evaluation states
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the asymptotic convergence improvement O(M^-1) vs O(M^-1/2); the example simulation is resolution-limited and does not always return the closest probability.

speedup_claims.conditions: across 1 to 19 evaluation qubits; comparing IonQ trapped-ion hardware to IBM superconducting devices
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a circuit-resource reduction, not a runtime or accuracy speedup; exact IBM counts depend on backend topology and qubit placement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(M^-1) estimation error for QAE, with M = 2^n evaluation states

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; only circuit-resource scaling and a toy p=0.2 example are reported
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: More evaluation qubits increase QAE resolution, but the paper only reports two-qubit gate counts and simulator output; no end-to-end runtime or accuracy advantage over classical methods is demonstrated
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup is only asymptotic and not benchmarked against a full classical implementation
Results are limited to a simplified single-period bond example
Hardware overhead from two-qubit gates and SWAP routing dominates on superconducting devices
No error-corrected or large-scale QPU demonstration

notes: Hardware is reported as IBM QASM simulator for the example simulation, while the scalability study also reports IBM superconducting and IonQ trapped-ion gate decompositions; the experiment is treated as a single gate-based QAE scalability study.
num_qubits is reported as varying from 1 to 19 evaluation qubits, with a 4-qubit example for p=0.2 and 3 evaluation qubits.
Circuit depth is not explicitly reported; only two-qubit gate counts and polynomial fits are given.
The paper reports asymptotic QAE convergence O(M^-1) versus classical Monte Carlo O(M^-1/2), but does not demonstrate practical end-to-end advantage.
The empirical result is a circuit-resource comparison across IBM and IonQ hardware, not a classical-vs-quantum performance win.

experiments.description: Hardware-specific circuit resource comparison for the same QAE circuit on IBM Yorktown, IBM Tokyo, IBM Cairo, IBM ideal all-to-all superconducting model, and IonQ trapped-ion hardware.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Same QAE state preparation as exp_1

key_results: IBM ideal: 12 two-qubit gates for 3 evaluation qubits; scaling n^2 + n
IBM Yorktown: 15 two-qubit gates for 3 evaluation qubits due to one SWAP
IBM Tokyo: 12 two-qubit gates in favorable placement, 23 with one SWAP
IonQ: 9 two-qubit gates for 3 evaluation qubits; scaling n^2
